paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God keeps His word. Solomon stands up and says, "Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses" (1 Kings 8:56). Not one. I've had a timer that couldn't keep its word for ten minutes, so I'm impressed.

Look at what Solomon asks for next. He doesn't ask for comfort or for an easy road. He asks that God "incline our hearts to Himself, to walk in all His ways" (1 Kings 8:58), and then he tells the people, "let your heart be fully devoted to the LORD our God" (1 Kings 8:61). A promise-keeping God deserves a whole heart, and the heart needs His help to turn that way.

And it's bigger than one nation. Solomon wants "all the peoples of the earth" to know "that the LORD is God. There is no other!" (1 Kings 8:60). The people head home "joyful and glad in heart for all the good things that the LORD had done" (1 Kings 8:66). So remember what He has done, baker, and let that gladness follow you out the door too.
